source_text: Διὰ τοῦτο τὸν ζῳοφόρον λεγόμενον κύκλον διελόντες εἰς δώδεκα μέρη, ἐπειδὴ διὰ τριάκοντα ἡμερῶν ἐκβαίνει τὸ δωδέκατον τῆς ἀπλανοῦς λεγομένης σφαίρας ὁ ἥλιος, εἰς τριάκοντα μοίρας τῶν δωδεκατημορίων ἕκαστον διῃρήκασιν. Εἶτα ἑκάστην μοῖραν εἰς ἑξήκοντα διελόντες, ἕκαστον πάλιν τῶν ἑξηκοστῶν ἑξηκοντάκις ἔτεμον. Τιθέντες τοίνυν τὰς γενέσεις τῶν τικτομένων, ἴδωμεν εἰ τὴν ἀκρίβειαν ταύτην τῆς τοῦ χρόνου διαιρέσεως ἀποσῶσαι δυνήσονται. Ὁμοῦ τε γὰρ ἐτέχθη τὸ παιδίον, καὶ ἡ μαῖα κατασκοπεῖ τὸ γεννηθὲν ἄρρεν ἢ θῆλυ· εἶτα ἀναμένει τὸν κλαυθμὸν, ὅπερ σημεῖόν ἐστι τῆς ζωῆς τοῦ τεχθέντος. Πόσα βούλει ἐν τούτῳ τῷ χρόνῳ παραδραμεῖν ἑξηκοστά; Εἶπε τῷ Χαλδαίῳ τὸ γεννηθέν. Διὰ πόσων, βούλει, θῶμεν τῶν λεπτοτάτων τῆς μαίας τὴν φωνὴν παρελθεῖν· ἄλλως τε καὶ εἰ τύχοι ἔξω τῆς γυναικωνίτιδος ἑστὼς ὁ τὴν ὥραν ἀποτιθέμενος; Δεῖ γὰρ τὸν τὰ ὡροσκοπεῖα καταμαθεῖν μέλλοντα, πρὸς ἀκρίβειαν τὴν ὥραν ἀπογράφεσθαι, εἴτε ἡμερινὰ ταῦτα, εἴτε νυκτερινὰ τυγχάνοι. Πόσων ἑξηκοστῶν σμῆνος ἐν τούτῳ πάλιν παρα τρέχει τῷ χρόνῳ; Ἀνάγκη γὰρ εὑρεθῆναι τὸν ὡροσκοποῦντα ἀστέρα οὐ μόνον κατὰ πόστου δωδεκατημορίου ἐστὶν, ἀλλὰ καὶ κατὰ ποίας μοίρας τοῦ δωδεκατημορίου, καὶ ἐν πόστῳ ἑξηκοστῷ, εἰς ἃ ἔφαμεν διαιρεῖσθαι τὴν μοῖραν· ἢ, ἵνα τὸ ἀκριβὲς εὑρεθῇ, ἐν πόστῳ ἑξηκοστῷ τῶν ὑποδιῃρημένων ἀπὸ τῶν πρώτων ἑξηκοστῶν. Καὶ ταύτην τὴν οὕτω λεπτὴν καὶ ἀκατάληπτον εὕρεσιν τοῦ χρόνου ἐφ' ἑκάστου τῶν πλανητῶν ἀναγκαῖον εἶναι ποιεῖσθαι λέγουσιν, ὥστε εὑρεθῆναι ποταπὴν εἶχον σχέσιν πρὸς τοὺς ἀπλανεῖς, καὶ ποταπὸν ἦν τὸ σχῆμα αὐτῶν πρὸς ἀλλήλους ἐν τῇ τότε γενέσει τοῦ τικτομένου. Ὥστε εἰ τῆς ὥρας ἐπιτυχεῖν ἀκριβῶς ἀδύνατον, ἡ δὲ τοῦ βραχυτάτου παραλλαγὴ τοῦ παντὸς διαμαρτεῖν ποιεῖ, καταγέλαστοι καὶ οἱ περὶ τὴν ἐνύπαρκτον ταύτην τέχνην ἐσχολακότες, καὶ οἱ πρὸς αὐτοὺς κεχηνότες, ὡς δυναμένους εἰδέναι τὰ κατ' αὐτούς. 6.6 Οἷα δὲ καὶ τὰ ἀποτελεστικά; Ὁ δεῖνα οὖλος, φησὶ, τὴν τρίχα, καὶ χαροπός· κριῷ γὰρ ἔχει τὴν ὥραν· τοιοῦτον δέ πως ὀφθῆναι τὸ ζῷον. Ἀλλὰ καὶ μεγαλόφρων· ἐπειδὴ ἡγεμονικὸν ὁ κριός· καὶ προετικὸς, καὶ πάλιν ποριστικός· ἐπειδὴ τὸ ζῷον τοῦτο καὶ ἀποτίθεται ἀλύπως τὸ ἔριον, καὶ πάλιν παρὰ τῆς φύσεως ῥᾳδίως ἐπαμφιέννυται. Ἀλλὰ καὶ ὁ ταυριανὸς τληπαθὴς, φησὶ, καὶ δουλικός· ἐπειδὴ ὑπὸ ζυγὸν ὁ ταῦρος. Καὶ ὁ σκορπιανὸς πλήκτης διὰ τὴν πρὸς τὸ θηρίον ὁμοίωσιν. Ὁ δὲ ζυγιανὸς δίκαιος, διὰ τὴν παρ' ἡμῖν τῶν ζυγῶν ἰσότητα. Τούτων τί ἂν γένοιτο καταγελαστότερον; Ὁ κριὸς, ἀφ' οὗ τὴν γένεσιν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου λαμβάνεις, οὐρανοῦ μέρος ἐστὶ τὸ δωδέκατον, ἐν ᾧ γενόμενος ὁ ἥλιος τῶν ἐαρινῶν σημείων ἅπτεται. Καὶ ζυγὸς, καὶ ταῦρος ὡσαύτως, ἕκαστον τούτων δωδεκατημόριόν ἐστι τοῦ ζῳδιακοῦ λεγομένου κύκλου. Πῶς οὖν ἐκεῖθεν τὰς προηγουμένας αἰτίας λέγων ὑπάρχειν τοῖς τῶν ἀνθρώπων βίοις, ἐκ τῶν παρ' ἡμῖν βοσκημάτων τῶν γεν νωμένων ἀνθρώπων τὰ ἤθη χαρακτηρίζεις; Εὐμετάδοτος γὰρ ὁ κριανὸς, οὐκ ἐπειδὴ τοιούτου ἤθους ποιητικὸν ἐκεῖνο τὸ μέρος τοῦ οὐρανοῦ, ἀλλ' ἐπειδὴ τοιαύτης φύσεώς ἐστι τὸ πρόβατον. Τί οὖν δυσωπεῖς μὲν ἡμᾶς ἀπὸ τῆς ἀξιοπιστίας τῶν ἄστρων, πείθειν δὲ ἐπιχειρεῖς διὰ τῶν βληχημάτων; Εἰ μὲν γὰρ παρὰ τῶν ζῴων λαβὼν ὁ οὐρανὸς ἔχει τὰ τοιαῦ τα τῶν ἠθῶν ἰδιώματα, καὶ αὐτὸς ὑπόκειται ἀλλοτρίαις ἀρχαῖς, ἐκ τῶν βοσκημάτων ἔχων τὰς αἰτίας ἀπηρτημένας· εἰ δὲ καταγέλαστον τοῦτο εἰπεῖν, καταγελαστότερον πολλῷ ἐκ τῶν μηδὲν κοινωνούντων ἐπάγειν ἐπιχειρεῖν τῷ λόγῳ τὰς πιθανότητας.
thought_title: Astrology's absurd precision and its animal logic
orientation: Basil is refuting astrology by showing that its own demand for exact birth-times is impossible, and then mocking its use of zodiac animals to explain human character.
pass_a_gloss: For this reason, having divided the circle called the zodiac into twelve parts, since in thirty days the sun passes through the twelfth part of the sphere called the fixed sphere, they have divided each of the twelfth-parts into thirty degrees. Then, having divided each degree into sixty, they cut each of the sixtieths again sixty times. So, when they set down the births of those being born, let us see whether they will be able to preserve this precision of the division of time. For at the same time the child was born, and the midwife examines whether the newborn is male or female; then she waits for the cry, which is a sign of the life of the one born. How many sixtieths do you want to have passed by in this time? Tell the Chaldean that the child has been born. Through how many, do you want, of the finest divisions shall we suppose the midwife's voice to pass; especially if the one recording the hour happens to be standing outside the women's quarters? For the one who is about to learn the horoscopes must record the hour with precision, whether these happen to be by day or by night. What swarm of sixtieths again passes by in this time? For it is necessary that the star marking the hour be found not only in which twelfth-part it is, but also in which degree of the twelfth-part, and in which sixtieth, into which we said the degree is divided; or, in order that the precise point be found, in which sixtieth of those subdivided from the first sixtieths. And they say it is necessary to make this so fine and incomprehensible finding of the time for each of the planets, so that it be found what relation they had to the fixed stars, and what was their configuration toward one another at the then birth of the one being born. So that if it is impossible to hit upon the hour precisely, and the variation of the very briefest moment makes one miss the whole, laughable are both those who have devoted themselves to this non-existent art, and those who gape at them, as though they were able to know the things concerning themselves. 6.6 And what sort of things are the results? So-and-so, he says, has curly hair and bright eyes; for he has the Ram for his hour; and the animal is seen somehow like that. But also high-minded; because the Ram is a leader; and open-handed, and again acquisitive; because this animal both puts off its wool without pain, and again is easily clothed by nature. But also the one born under the Bull is hardy, he says, and slavish; because the bull is under the yoke. And the one born under the Scorpion is a striker because of the likeness to the beast. And the one born under the Scales is just, because of the equality of the scales among us. What could be more laughable than these things? The Ram, from which you take the birth of the man, is a twelfth part of heaven, in which the sun being present touches the spring signs. And the Scales, and the Bull likewise, each of these is a twelfth-part of the circle called the zodiac. How then, saying that the primary causes for the lives of men exist from there, do you characterize the characters of men born from the cattle among us? For the one born under the Ram is open-handed, not because that part of heaven is productive of such a character, but because the sheep is of such a nature. Why then do you awe us with the trustworthiness of the stars, and attempt to persuade us through bleatings? For if the heaven, having received from the animals, has such peculiarities of characters, it too is subject to alien principles, having its causes dependent on the cattle; but if it is laughable to say this, it is much more laughable to attempt to bring in plausibilities for the argument from things that have nothing in common.

choices.why: Keeps the literal 'animal-bearing' sense of ζῳοφόρος while using the standard English term; 'called' preserves λεγόμενον.

choices.english: the sphere called the fixed sphere
choices.why: ἀπλανής means 'not wandering,' i.e., fixed; keeping 'fixed sphere' preserves the literal contrast with planets (wanderers).
ἀποτίθεσθαι here means 'to set down, record' in writing; 'recording' captures the technical act of noting the birth hour.
rejected: the one laying down the hour

choices.english: the one born under the Ram
choices.why: The rare form κριανός means a person whose birth sign is the Ram; this rendering matches Basil's style and avoids modern astrological jargon.
προετικός derives from προΐημι, 'to give forth'; 'open-handed' captures the sense of giving freely and bountifully.
βλήχημα is literally 'bleating'; Basil uses it metonymically for the sheep themselves, and the literal rendering preserves the rhetorical contempt of the question.

pass_b_english: For this reason they divided the circle called the zodiac into twelve parts, and because the sun passes through one twelfth of the sphere called the fixed sphere in thirty days, they divided each of the twelfth-parts into thirty degrees. Then they divided each degree into sixty parts, and each of those sixtieths they cut again sixty times. So when they set down the births of children, let us see whether they can preserve this precision in dividing time. For the child is born, and at the same moment the midwife examines whether the newborn is male or female; then she waits for the cry, which is the sign that the child is alive. How many sixtieths do you suppose pass by in that time? Then she tells the Chaldean that the child has been born. Through how many of the very finest divisions, do you suppose, the midwife's voice travels—especially if the one who is supposed to fix the hour happens to be standing outside the women's quarters? For the one who intends to study horoscopes must record the hour with precision, whether it is by day or by night. What a swarm of sixtieths passes by again in that time! For it is necessary, they say, to determine not only in which twelfth-part the star that marks the hour is, but also in which degree of that twelfth-part, and in which sixtieth—into which we said the degree is divided—or, to find the exact point, in which sixtieth of the subdivisions of the first sixtieths. And they say it is necessary to make this extremely fine and incomprehensible determination of time for each of the planets, so as to find what relation they had to the fixed stars, and what configuration they had toward one another at the moment of the child's birth. So if it is impossible to hit upon the hour exactly, and the variation of the very briefest moment causes one to miss everything, then both those who have devoted themselves to this non-existent art are ridiculous, and so are those who gape at them as though they could know what concerns them. 6.6 And what are the results like? 'So-and-so,' he says, 'is curly-haired and bright-eyed, for he has the Ram as his ascendant; for the animal is seen somewhat like that.' But he is also high-minded, because the Ram is a leader; and open-handed, and again resourceful, because this animal both sheds its wool without pain and is easily clothed again by nature. 'But the one born under the Bull,' he says, 'is hardy and servile, because the bull is under the yoke.' And the one born under the Scorpion is a striker, because of his likeness to the beast. The one born under the Scales is just, because of the equality of scales among us. What could be more ridiculous than these things? The Ram, from which you take the birth of a human being, is a twelfth part of heaven, in which the sun comes to touch the signs of spring. And the Scales and the Bull likewise—each of these is a twelfth-part of the circle called the zodiac. How then, when you say that the primary causes for human lives exist, do you characterize the characters of people born from our domestic animals? For the one born under the Ram is open-handed, not because that part of heaven produces such a character, but because the sheep has such a nature. Why then do you try to overawe us with the authority of the stars, while attempting to persuade us through bleatings? For if heaven received such peculiarities of character from the animals, then heaven itself is subject to alien principles, having its causes derived from cattle. But if it is ridiculous to say this, it is far more ridiculous to try to bring into the argument plausibilities drawn from things that have nothing in common with it.

problems.quote: the one recording the hour happens to be standing outside the women's quarters
problems.source_quote: ἄλλως τε καὶ εἰ τύχοι ἔξω τῆς γυναικωνίτιδος ἑστὼς ὁ τὴν ὥραν ἀποτιθέμενος
problems.why: ἀποτιθέμενος means 'laying aside/setting down' (the hour), not 'recording'; the astrologer is the one failing to note the hour, not actively recording it.
problems.fix: the one who is supposed to fix the hour happens to be standing outside the women's quarters

problems.quote: because he has the Ram as his hour
problems.why: ἔχει τὴν ὥραν means 'has the hour/ascendant in Aries', not 'has the Ram as his hour'; the technical astrological sense of ὥρα as 'ascendant/hour-marker' is lost.
problems.fix: for he has the Ram as his ascendant
problems.ruling: κριῷ ἔχει τὴν ὥραν = 'has the hour in the Ram'; 'has the Ram as his hour' inverts the technical sense.
